info.name: linkMe API
info.description: Auth v1 endpoints for the linkMe backend (see DOCS/authentication_v1_backend_spec.md and DOCS/postman.md for the full testing walkthrough, especially for confirming emails actually send).

request.description: 200 OK, plain text "ok". Public, no rate limit.

201 Created. Body: {id, email, expires_at}. Registration intentionally collects ONLY email + password — no name, no profile fields; those are set afterward via PATCH /api/v1/me/profile (see the Update Profile request below). Sets access_token + refresh_token HttpOnly cookies — this request's test script reads them via pm.cookies.get(...) and stores them in the access_token/refresh_token collection variables automatically. Rate limit: 5/hour. 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS if test_email is already registered and not deleted — just Login instead. If test_email belongs to a previously-deleted account, this instead REACTIVATES it (clears deleted_at, sets the password to whatever you send here) and signs you in — see Delete Account's description. Password must satisfy the policy: 12–72 bytes, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one digit, one special character — a non-conforming password returns 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS. An unrecognized JSON field (e.g. a stray "name") now returns 400 INVALID_BODY — the server rejects unknown fields instead of silently ignoring them.

200 OK, same body/cookie shape as Register. 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS covers unknown email, wrong password, a deleted account, and OAuth-only accounts identically (enumeration defense — none of these are distinguishable from the response). Rate limit: 10/15min.

200 OK. Body: {expires_at}. The handler reads the refresh token from a Cookie header (not Authorization) — sent explicitly above from the refresh_token variable rather than relying on Postman's cookie jar to resend a Secure cookie over plain http. Rotates both tokens (this request's test script re-captures them). Running Refresh twice with the same now-stale refresh_token triggers reuse detection: 401 TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED and the whole session family is revoked. Rate limit: 60/15min.
204 No Content. Revokes the current session (identified by the access token's session claim) and is idempotent. Requires RequireAuth. Rate limit: 10/15min.
204 No Content. Revokes every active session for the user. Requires RequireAuth. Rate limit: 5/15min.

Redirects (302) to Google's consent screen and sets a short-lived signed oauth_state cookie. Not a JSON endpoint — open in a browser rather than running via Postman's test runner. Rate limit: 10/15min.

Google redirects here after consent with ?code=&state=. Validates the oauth_state cookie against state, exchanges code, and on success sets the same access_token/refresh_token cookies as Login before redirecting (302) to FRONTEND_URL. On failure redirects to FRONTEND_URL?error=oauth_failed or ?error=oauth_state_invalid. Not directly usable from Postman's test runner — exercise the full flow in a browser starting from Google: Start. Rate limit: 10/15min.

200 OK. Body: {data: {id, email, email_verified, name, avatar_url, company_name, description, social_links: {platforms, other}, has_password, plan: {id, status}}}. name/avatar_url/company_name/description are omitted until set via Update Profile. has_password is never omitted (always present, true/false) — the frontend uses it to decide whether to show "change password" (has one) or "set a password" (doesn't, e.g. an OAuth-only account). Requires RequireAuth. Rate limit: 60/15min.

204 No Content. Verifies current_password, hashes new_password (must satisfy the password policy: 12–72 bytes, upper+lower+digit+special), and revokes every OTHER active session (this one stays alive). 401 PASSWORD_NOT_SET-style rejection doesn't apply here since this route requires an existing password (use Set Password instead for an OAuth-only account with none). Requires RequireAuth. Rate limit: 5/15min. After running this, either update test_password to match new_password, or use new_password directly on the next Login.

204 No Content. Sets an INITIAL password on an account that doesn't have one yet (e.g. an account created via Google sign-in) — unlike Change Password, this never verifies a current password, since there isn't one. Meaningful test requires an OAuth-only account: sign in via Google: Start in a real browser (see §5 below), grab the access_token cookie it sets, and use that here instead of {{access_token}}. Revokes every OTHER active session after setting it, same safety property as Change Password. 409 PASSWORD_ALREADY_SET if the account already has a password (use Change Password instead). 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS if new_password fails the policy. Requires RequireAuth. Rate limit: 5/15min. Run Get Me afterward — has_password flips from false to true.

200 OK. Body: {data: <same shape as Get Me>}. PARTIAL PATCH — every field is optional; omit a field to leave it unchanged, or send an empty string/object to clear it. Delete any field you don't want to touch from the raw JSON before sending (this example sends all of them for demonstration). social_links.platforms keys must be one of: website, x, instagram, youtube, tiktok, discord, github, linkedin — an unrecognized key (e.g. a typo like "diskord") returns 400 INVALID_INPUT rather than being silently stored, so the frontend can always map a known key to a brand icon. social_links.other is a free-text {label, url} list for anything not in that enum (max 5 entries). All URLs must be http(s). 400 INVALID_INPUT for any validation failure (bad URL, unknown platform, too many custom links, control characters in text fields, etc). Requires RequireAuth. Rate limit: 20/15min.

204 No Content. DESTRUCTIVE — run this last, deliberately, not as part of a normal test pass. current_password MUST match whatever the account's password actually is right now (it may have changed if you ran Change Password or Confirm Password Reset earlier — update this field to match, or re-run Login first to confirm which password currently works). Ignored entirely for an OAuth-only account (has_password: false) — being authenticated is enough, no password needed. Soft-deletes the account (deleted_at set), revokes every session, clears cookies. 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS if current_password doesn't match. The account and its email are NOT purged — users.email stays permanently unique, so nobody (including you) can register a brand-new account with test_email again. Instead, running Register again with test_email REACTIVATES this same account: clears deleted_at, sets the password to whatever Register was called with, and signs you in — try it right after this to see the restore flow. Requires RequireAuth. Rate limit: 5/15min.

200 OK ALWAYS, regardless of whether the email exists or is already verified (enumeration defense) — body: {data: {message: "..."}}. This is where the actual email send happens. See DOCS/postman.md §"Did we actually send an email?" for how to check the Resend dashboard and grab the token for the next request. Rate limit: 5/hour — don't spam this while testing.

Set the verification_token collection variable to the raw token from the email link (or the Resend dashboard preview) before running this. 200 OK: {data: <same shape as Get Me>}, with email_verified now true. 401 TOKEN_INVALID if unknown/expired, 401 TOKEN_ALREADY_USED if already consumed. Rate limit: 10/15min.

200 OK ALWAYS: {data: {message: "If an account exists, a password reset email has been sent."}} — enumeration defense, matches the auth spec's example verbatim. Check the Resend dashboard for the actual token, same as email verification. Rate limit: 5/hour.

204 No Content. Revokes ALL sessions for the account, including the one behind {{access_token}} — re-run Login afterward with new_password. 401 TOKEN_INVALID/TOKEN_ALREADY_USED, 400 PASSWORD_NOT_SET for OAuth-only accounts, 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS if new_password is weak. Rate limit: 10/15min.
